content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

segments.t: Canticum Trium Puerorum

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.latin: Ant. Facta est cum Angelo multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

Facta est cum Angelo multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúia, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúia, allelúia.

content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.english: At Rome, the birthday of St. Felix I, pope and martyr, who governed the Church during the reign of Emperor Aurelian. His feast day is celebrated on the 30th of May.

content.latin: Spoléti item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sabíni, Assisiénsis Epíscopi, atque Exsuperántii et Marcélli Diaconórum, ac Venustiáni Prǽsidis cum uxóre et fíliis, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre. Ex ipsis Marcéllus et Exsuperántius, primum equúleo suspénsi, deínde fústibus gráviter mactáti, postrémum, abrási úngulis et láterum exustióne assáti, martýrium complevérunt; Venustiánus autem non multo post, simul cum uxóre et fíliis, est gládio necátus; sanctus vero Sabínus, post detruncatiónem mánuum et diútinam cárceris maceratiónem, ad mortem usque cæsus est. Horum martýrium, licet divérso exstíterit témpore, una tamen die recólitur.
content.english: At Spoleto, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Sabinus, bishop of that see; the deacons Exuperantius and Marcellus, and the President Venustian along with his wife and children. Marcellus and Exuperantius were first racked then heavily cudgelled, then mangled with hooks, and their sides were afterwards burnt until they died. Venustian and his wife and children were shortly afterward put to the sword holy Sabinus had his hands cut off, and was long imprisoned, and at length lashed to death. These did not all suffer at the same time, but they are all commemorated upon the same day.

segments.t: Psalmus 39(2-9)

content.latin: 39:2 Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
content.english: 39:2 With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

segments.t: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.

content.latin: 39:3 Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
content.english: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

segments.t: Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.

content.latin: 39:3 Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
content.english: 39:3 And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

segments.t: Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.

content.latin: 39:4 Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
content.english: 39:4 And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

segments.t: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.

content.latin: 39:4 Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
content.english: 39:4 Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

segments.t: Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.

content.latin: 39:5 Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
content.english: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.

content.latin: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
content.english: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

segments.t: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.

content.latin: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
content.english: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

segments.t: Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.

content.latin: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
content.english: 39:7 Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

segments.t: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.

content.latin: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
content.english: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

segments.t: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.

content.latin: 39:8 In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
content.english: 39:8 In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

segments.t: In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Psalmus 39(10-14)

content.latin: 39:10 Annuntiávi iustítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
content.english: 39:10 I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

segments.t: Annuntiávi iustítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.

content.latin: 39:11 Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
content.english: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

segments.t: Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.

content.latin: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
content.english: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

segments.t: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.

content.latin: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
content.english: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.

content.latin: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
content.english: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

segments.t: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.

content.latin: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
content.english: 39:13 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.

content.latin: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

segments.t: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.

Psalmus 39(15-18)

content.latin: 39:15 Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

segments.t: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.

content.latin: 39:15 Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

segments.t: Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.

content.latin: 39:16 Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
content.english: 39:16 Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

segments.t: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.latin: 39:17 Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
content.english: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
content.english: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

segments.t: Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.

content.latin: 39:18 Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
content.english: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

segments.t: Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.

content.latin: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
content.english: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti iugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
content.english: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the new birth of thy Only-begotten Son as man may set us free, who are held by the old bondage under the yoke of sin.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.english: Psalm 40 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 40

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

segments.t: Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

segments.t: Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

segments.t: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

segments.t: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

segments.t: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

segments.t: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

segments.t: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

segments.t: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

segments.t: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

segments.t: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

segments.t: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

segments.t: Psalmus 43(2-9)

content.latin: 43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
content.english: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

segments.t: Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.

content.latin: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
content.english: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

segments.t: Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

segments.t: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
content.english: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

segments.t: Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:

content.latin: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
content.english: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

segments.t: Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.

content.latin: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.
content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

segments.t: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
content.english: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

segments.t: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.

content.latin: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
content.english: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

segments.t: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
content.english: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

segments.t: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.

Psalmus 43(10-20)

content.latin: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
content.english: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

segments.t: Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.

content.latin: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
content.english: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

segments.t: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.

content.latin: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
content.english: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

segments.t: Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.

content.latin: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
content.english: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

segments.t: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.

content.latin: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
content.english: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

segments.t: Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.

content.latin: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

segments.t: Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.

content.latin: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
content.english: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

segments.t: Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.

content.latin: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
content.english: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

segments.t: A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
content.english: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

segments.t: Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.

content.latin: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
content.english: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

segments.t: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:

content.latin: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
content.english: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.

content.english: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

content.english: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

segments.t: Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.

content.latin: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
content.english: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

segments.t: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.

content.latin: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
content.english: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

segments.t: Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.

content.latin: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
content.english: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

segments.t: Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?

content.latin: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
content.english: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.

content.latin: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
content.english: 43:26 Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.

content.latin: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

content.latin: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti iugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
content.english: Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that the new birth of thy Only-begotten Son as man may set us free, who are held by the old bondage under the yoke of sin.

content.latin: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 109

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

segments.t: Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

segments.t: Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

segments.t: Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

segments.t: Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

segments.t: Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

segments.t: De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.

content.latin: Psalmus 110 [2]
content.english: Psalm 110 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 110

content.latin: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
content.english: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.

content.latin: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
content.english: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

segments.t: Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.

content.latin: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.

segments.t: Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.

content.latin: 110:5 Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
content.english: 110:5 He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

segments.t: Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:

content.latin: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
content.english: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

segments.t: Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.

content.latin: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
content.english: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

segments.t: Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.

content.latin: 110:9 Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
content.english: 110:9 He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

segments.t: Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.

content.latin: 110:9 (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
content.english: 110:9 (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

segments.t: 110:9 (fit reverentia)
Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.

content.latin: 110:10 Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:10 A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Psalmus 111 [3]
content.english: Psalm 111 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 111

content.latin: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.
content.english: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.

content.latin: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
content.english: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

segments.t: Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.

content.latin: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.
content.english: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

segments.t: Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.

content.latin: 111:5 Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
content.english: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment: * because he shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.

content.latin: 111:7 In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
content.english: 111:7 The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

segments.t: In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.

content.latin: 111:7 Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
content.english: 111:7 His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

segments.t: Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.

content.latin: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.
content.english: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

segments.t: Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.

content.latin: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
content.english: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.

content.english: Ant. With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

content.latin: Psalmus 129 [4]
content.english: Psalm 129 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 129

content.latin: 129:1 De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
content.english: 129:1 Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.

segments.t: De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:

content.latin: 129:2 Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 129:2 Let thy ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

segments.t: Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.

content.latin: 129:3 Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
content.english: 129:3 If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it.

segments.t: Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?

content.latin: 129:4 Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
content.english: 129:4 For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: * and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.

content.latin: 129:5 Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo eius: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
content.english: 129:5 My soul hath relied on his word: * my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

segments.t: Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo eius: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.

content.latin: 129:6 A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
content.english: 129:6 From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.

segments.t: A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.

content.latin: 131:1 Meménto, Dómine, David, * et omnis mansuetúdinis eius:

segments.t: Meménto, Dómine, David, * et omnis mansuetúdinis eius:

content.latin: 131:2 Sicut iurávit Dómino, * votum vovit Deo Iacob:
content.english: 131:2 How he swore to the Lord, * he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob:

segments.t: Sicut iurávit Dómino, * votum vovit Deo Iacob:

content.latin: 131:3 Si introíero in tabernáculum domus meæ, * si ascéndero in lectum strati mei:
content.english: 131:3 If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house: * if I shall go up into the bed wherein I lie:

segments.t: Si introíero in tabernáculum domus meæ, * si ascéndero in lectum strati mei:

content.latin: 131:4 Si dédero somnum óculis meis, * et pálpebris meis dormitatiónem:
content.english: 131:4 If I shall give sleep to my eyes, * or slumber to my eyelids,

segments.t: Si dédero somnum óculis meis, * et pálpebris meis dormitatiónem:

content.latin: 131:5 Et réquiem tempóribus meis: donec invéniam locum Dómino, * tabernáculum Deo Iacob.
content.english: 131:5 Or rest to my temples: until I find out a place for the Lord, * a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Et réquiem tempóribus meis: donec invéniam locum Dómino, * tabernáculum Deo Iacob.

content.latin: 131:6 Ecce, audívimus eam in Éphrata: * invénimus eam in campis silvæ.
content.english: 131:6 Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: * we have found it in the fields of the wood.

segments.t: Ecce, audívimus eam in Éphrata: * invénimus eam in campis silvæ.

content.latin: 131:7 Introíbimus in tabernáculum eius: * adorábimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes eius.
content.english: 131:7 We will go into his tabernacle: * we will adore in the place where his feet stood.

segments.t: Introíbimus in tabernáculum eius: * adorábimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes eius.

content.latin: 131:8 Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, * tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 131:8 Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place: * thou and the ark, which thou hast sanctified.

segments.t: Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, * tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.

content.latin: 131:9 Sacerdótes tui induántur iustítiam: * et sancti tui exsúltent.
content.english: 131:9 Let thy priests be clothed with justice: * and let thy saints rejoice.

segments.t: Sacerdótes tui induántur iustítiam: * et sancti tui exsúltent.

content.latin: 131:10 Propter David, servum tuum, * non avértas fáciem Christi tui.
content.english: 131:10 For thy servant David’s sake, * turn not away the face of thy anointed.

segments.t: Propter David, servum tuum, * non avértas fáciem Christi tui.

content.latin: 131:11 Iurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: * De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
content.english: 131:11 The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: * of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: * De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.

content.latin: 131:12 Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:
content.english: 131:12 If thy children will keep my covenant, * and these my testimonies which I shall teach them:

segments.t: Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:

content.latin: 131:12 Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum, * sedébunt super sedem tuam.
content.english: 131:12 Their children also for evermore * shall sit upon thy throne.

segments.t: Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum, * sedébunt super sedem tuam.

content.latin: 131:13 Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.
content.english: 131:13 For the Lord hath chosen Sion: * he hath chosen it for his dwelling.

segments.t: Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.

content.latin: 131:14 Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.
content.english: 131:14 This is my rest for ever and ever: * here will I dwell, for I have chosen it.

segments.t: Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.

content.latin: 131:15 Víduam eius benedícens benedícam: * páuperes eius saturábo pánibus.
content.english: 131:15 Blessing I will bless her widow: * I will satisfy her poor with bread.

segments.t: Víduam eius benedícens benedícam: * páuperes eius saturábo pánibus.

content.latin: 131:16 Sacerdótes eius índuam salutári: * et sancti eius exsultatióne exsultábunt.
content.english: 131:16 I will clothe her priests with salvation: * and her saints shall rejoice with exceeding great joy.

segments.t: Sacerdótes eius índuam salutári: * et sancti eius exsultatióne exsultábunt.

content.latin: 131:17 Illuc prodúcam cornu David, * parávi lucérnam Christo meo.
content.english: 131:17 There will I bring forth a horn to David: * I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.

segments.t: Illuc prodúcam cornu David, * parávi lucérnam Christo meo.

content.latin: 131:18 Inimícos eius índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.
content.english: 131:18 His enemies I will clothe with confusion: * but upon him shall my sanctification flourish.

segments.t: Inimícos eius índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere:

content.latin: Misereátur nostri omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis nostris, perdúcat nos ad vitam ætérnam. Amen.
content.english: May almighty God have mercy on us, forgive us our sins, and bring us to everlasting life. Amen.

content.latin: Indulgéntiam, ✠ absolutiónem et remissiónem peccatórum nostrórum tríbuat nobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus. Amen.
content.english: May the almighty ✠ and merciful Lord grant us pardon, absolution and remission of our sins. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Convérte nos ✙︎ Deus, salutáris noster.
content.english: ℣. Turn us then, ✙︎ O God, our saviour:

segments.t: Convérte nos ✙︎ Deus, salutáris noster.

content.english: ℟. And let thy anger cease from us.

segments.t: Et avérte iram tuam a nobis.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Psalm 4 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 4

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

segments.t: Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.

content.latin: 4:2 Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: 4:2 Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

segments.t: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

segments.t: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Psalmus 90 [2]
content.english: Psalm 90 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 90

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
content.english: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.

content.latin: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
content.english: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

segments.t: Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

segments.t: Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

segments.t: Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

segments.t: Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
content.english: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

segments.t: A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

segments.t: Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.

content.latin: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
content.english: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

segments.t: Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.

content.latin: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
content.english: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

segments.t: Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.

content.latin: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
content.english: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

segments.t: Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.

content.latin: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
content.english: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

segments.t: Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.

content.latin: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
content.english: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

segments.t: In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.

content.latin: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
content.english: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

segments.t: Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.

content.latin: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
content.english: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

segments.t: Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.

content.latin: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
content.english: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: * I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

segments.t: Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.

content.latin: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.
content.english: 90:16 I will fill him with length of days; * and I will shew him my salvation.

segments.t: Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.

content.english: 133:1 Behold now bless ye the Lord, * all ye servants of the Lord:

segments.t: Ecce nunc benedícite Dóminum, * omnes servi Dómini:

content.english: 133:1 Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

segments.t: In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.

content.english: 133:3 May the Lord out of Sion bless thee, * he that made heaven and earth.

content.latin: Te lucis ante términum,
content.english: Before the ending of the day,

content.latin: Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
content.english: Creator of the world, we pray

content.latin: Ut pro tua cleméntia
content.english: That with thy wonted favor thou

content.latin: Sis præsul et custódia.
content.english: Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

content.latin: Procul recédant sómnia,
content.english: From all ill dreams defend our eyes,

content.latin: Et nóctium phantásmata;
content.english: From nightly fears and fantasies;

content.latin: Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
content.english: Tread under foot our ghostly foe,

content.latin: Ne polluántur córpora.
content.english: That no pollution we may know.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.

content.latin: Tu autem in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos, Dómine, Deus noster.
content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.english: ℣. Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

segments.t: Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.

content.english: ℟. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

segments.t: Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum. Amen.
content.english: O God, who, by the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary, hast bestowed upon mankind the reward of eternal salvation: grant, we beseech thee, that we may experience her intercession, through whom we have been made worthy to receive the author of life, Our Lord Jesus Christ thy Son. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

content.english: ℟. Amen.
